axes.decision: Duplicate establishment records (several GSS nominators naming the same establishment; copies carry V3 = 0)

levels.description: Keep all DS0002 records; each record is a case.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p6 (Data section counts responding 'organizations' with no mention of duplicates); NOS source description (duplicates documented)
levels.rationale: Closest to the article, which never mentions duplicate employers and treats every completed interview as an organization.

levels.description: Drop records with V3 = 0 (keep one record per distinct establishment).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: nos1991_source_description.md (documents that the file has more records than distinct establishments); standard practice for duplicated units
levels.rationale: Methodologically defensible and possibly what the authors did silently; changes N and the weight of repeated establishments. Cannot be resolved from the article.

axes.decision: Definition of the perceived-market-performance subsample

levels.description: Profit-making organizations: V8 = 1 (NOS Box F routes Q.76 only to profit-making organizations).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7 ('available only for profit-making organizations'); dictionary universe note for V296-V299
levels.rationale: Text statement matches the questionnaire routing.

levels.description: Publicly held corporations only: V8 = 1 and V9 = 4.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: D1 p10 Table 1 footnote a ('available only for publicly held firms'); D2 p9 identical
levels.rationale: Article-internal contradiction. A much smaller population; would change every Table 4 estimate. Flagged, not adopted.

axes.decision: Scope of listwise deletion

levels.description: One common complete-case sample per table over the outcome, all seven HRM indices, all controls and industry code; every model in the table uses it.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p15 and p17: identical N printed for every column of each table, including the single-practice regressions
levels.rationale: Only a common sample yields identical N across models that use different HRM variables.

levels.description: Model-specific complete cases (each regression keeps all cases non-missing on its own regressors).
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: Default software behaviour
levels.rationale: Would produce different N across models, contradicting the printed tables.

axes.decision: Index scoring when some items are structurally skipped or missing (POP, PMP, STAFF, TRAIN, INCENT, ILM, DECENT)

levels.description: Mean of the available (non-missing) items; establishment retained if at least one item is present.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7-8 ('averaged', 'standardized and averaged'); dictionary skip notes (GSS block skipped when GSS = CORE; manager block skipped when CORE/GSS is managerial)
levels.rationale: The only reading under which establishments whose GSS or manager block is skipped by design remain in the sample; the article describes averaging without any completeness requirement.

levels.description: Require all items non-missing; otherwise the index is missing.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Common psychometric practice (Nunnally & Bernstein 1994, cited D1 p11)
levels.rationale: Would remove a large share of establishments by design; not described, but not excluded by the text.

levels.description: Fill structurally skipped GSS/manager items with the CORE value (because the occupation is the same job).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: NOS questionnaire logic (Box A/B: block skipped because the occupation is identical to CORE)
levels.rationale: Substantively consistent with the skip reason; not described in the article.

axes.decision: Staffing selectivity: log transform and special codes of application counts (V62, V97, V131)

levels.description: Natural log of the count; codes 995, 997, 998, 999 set to missing.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7 ('logged value'); dictionary notes on codes 995/997
levels.rationale: Literal reading; 'natural logarithm' is the article's stated log elsewhere (D1 p11).

levels.description: log(1 + count) to retain zero counts.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Standard handling of zeros before logging
levels.rationale: Needed only if zero application counts occur; not described.

levels.description: Treat 995 'large number of applications' as a high substantive value (top code) rather than missing.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary: 995 is substantive but declared missing in the ICPSR file; NOS technical manual leaves missing decisions to users
levels.rationale: Affects the most selective establishments; article silent.

axes.decision: Sample on which standard scores (z-scores) for staffing and training items are computed

levels.description: Standardize within the final analysis sample of Table 3 (Sample A).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7 ('standard scores'); default practice
levels.rationale: Closest default; the article does not say.

levels.description: Standardize over all records with a non-missing item before any sample restriction.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: Linear rescaling of regressors: changes the index mean and scale by constants, so coefficients change by a scale factor and significance is unchanged
levels.rationale: Equivalent for sign and significance; coefficient magnitudes shift by the ratio of SDs. Flagged because Table 1 descriptive targets depend on it (see forensic F24).

axes.decision: Training index: log before standardizing

levels.description: Log each of the three items (dummy, count, effectiveness), then standardize and average.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p9-10 Table 1 footnote b attached to the 'Training effectiveness' heading: 'Standard score of logged value for all'
levels.rationale: The table footnote is explicit, although logging a 0/1 dummy is unusual (log(1 + x) would be required).

levels.description: Standardize the raw items (log only the participant count).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: D1 p7 text: 'These measures were standardized and averaged' (no log mentioned)
levels.rationale: Text-table conflict; monotone transformations of a dummy and a 3-point scale change the z-scores only slightly but not identically.

axes.decision: Training index: values for establishments with no formal training (V145 = no; V157 and V172 skipped)

levels.description: Assign zero participants and the lowest effectiveness category, then standardize (no-training establishments form the bottom of the index).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7: the index 'included a variable indicating whether the organization had provided any formal job training', which only discriminates if no-training establishments are in the sample; dictionary skip for Q.45a/Q.49
levels.rationale: Inferred, not stated; keeps the yes/no item meaningful.

levels.description: Index = mean of available standardized items (only the yes/no item for no-training establishments).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Same as A04 L0
levels.rationale: Alternative reading of 'averaged'.

levels.description: Treat skipped items as missing and drop the establishment.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: Dictionary routing
levels.rationale: Would remove every establishment without formal training, making the yes/no item constant; contradicts the index definition.

axes.decision: Decentralized decision making: mapping NOS response codes to the article's 1-5 scale

levels.description: Ordinal recode by locus of decision from above the establishment to below it: someone at larger org = 1, head and larger org = 2, head of org = 3, head and below = 4, someone below = 5; 'depends' and 7/8/9 missing. Q.72a and Q.72b item sets merged by V17.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: D1 p8 ('lowest value ... if the CEO makes these decisions and higher values ... someone lower'); Table 1 range 1-5 (D1 p10); dictionary codes for V271-V286
levels.rationale: Reproduces the 1-5 range and the stated direction for 'below' vs 'head', but places the larger organization below the head, which the text does not mention. No level is article-described; L0 is the placeholder origin.

levels.description: head of org = 1, head and larger org = 2, someone at larger org = 3, head and below = 4, someone below = 5.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Text statement that the CEO (head) value is the lowest
levels.rationale: Takes the 'lowest = CEO' statement literally; ordering of larger-org categories is arbitrary.

levels.description: Three-point recode (head only = 1, shared = 2, someone below = 3) with larger-org answers treated as missing.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: Methodological simplification
levels.rationale: Does not reproduce the printed 1-5 range.

axes.decision: Union pressure index: constituent NOS items

levels.description: Mean of V220 and V233 (importance of union negotiations for CORE and GSS earnings, reversed so higher = more important) and V300 (relations with unions as a problem, reversed so higher = bigger problem).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: D1 p12 (index of 'respondents' perception of the influence of unions on their organization', alpha reported, 'only measure of union influence available in the NOS'); dictionary search for union items
levels.rationale: These are the establishment-level perceptual union items in the NOS. No level is article-described; L0 is the placeholder origin.

levels.description: L0 items plus V166 (formal training offered because of union contracts, yes = 1).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary (Q.47b)
levels.rationale: Also a union-influence indicator, but only asked of establishments with formal training.

levels.description: V220 and V233 only (earnings-criteria items).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary (Q.63a, Q.65a share the same 1-3 response format)
levels.rationale: Homogeneous response format; plausible for a reliability-based index.

axes.decision: Subsidiary dummy: source item and orientation

levels.description: V17 = 1 (part of a larger organization) coded as the high category; independent establishments low.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p11 ('whether an organization is a subsidiary of another organization'); dictionary Q.4a
levels.rationale: Closest item; orientation implied by the label.

levels.description: V21 = 2 (wholly owned subsidiary) only; all others low.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary Q.4e category 'wholly owned subsidiary'
levels.rationale: Literal reading of 'subsidiary'; narrower group.

levels.description: V21 in {1, 2, 3} (branch, subsidiary, franchise) high; schools, campuses, government units and independents low.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary Q.4e
levels.rationale: Business-subsidiary reading; not described.

axes.decision: Firm age functional form

levels.description: Natural log of (1991 - V16).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p13 Table 2 row 13 and Tables 3-4 row 'Log of firm age'
levels.rationale: All tables label the variable as a log; the reported coefficients belong to this form.

levels.description: Age in years, 1991 - V16, unlogged.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: D1 p11 text ('the age of the firm in years')
levels.rationale: Article-internal conflict; a different functional form whose coefficient is not comparable to the printed one.

levels.description: Natural log of (1991 - V16 + 1) to accommodate establishments founded in 1991.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: Standard zero-handling
levels.rationale: Differs from L0 only for very young establishments; same construct and scale.

axes.decision: Total employment definition for log of total employment

levels.description: ln(V23 + V32), full-time plus part-time employees at the establishment.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p11 ('number of employees in the organization'); dictionary Q.5a
levels.rationale: Literal count of employees.

levels.description: ln(NEWTOTAL), the file's assigned total.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: Dictionary (NEWTOTAL = NEWFULL + NEWPART, assigned values used for weights)
levels.rationale: Same construct with imputed values for missing counts; differs only where Q.5a is missing.

levels.description: ln(V23), full-time employees only.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Q.5a wording distinguishes full-time (35+ hours)
levels.rationale: Not described; different scale for part-time-heavy establishments.

axes.decision: Percent managers: numerator when the manager block is skipped and denominator

levels.description: V115 / (V23 + V32); establishments with V114 = 3 (no managers) get 0; establishments whose managers are the CORE or GSS occupation (V114 = 2) use the corresponding CORE (V45) or GSS (V80) count as the numerator.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p12 ('percentage of employees in managerial occupations'); dictionary Q.29a-b and Box B
levels.rationale: Only reading that yields a defined share for every establishment; inferred.

levels.description: V115 / (V23 + V32); missing when V115 is skipped.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Dictionary routing
levels.rationale: Reduces the sample to establishments with a distinct manager group.

levels.description: Numerator as L0 but denominator NEWTOTAL.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: As A14 L1
levels.rationale: Same construct.

axes.decision: Market competition / competitive pressure coding

levels.description: V328 as a 1-4 scale (none to a great deal).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p12 ('1 = none, 4 = a great deal')
levels.rationale: Explicit text.

levels.description: Dummy = 1 if V328 = 4 (a great deal).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: D1 p13 Table 2 row 19 (mean and SD consistent with a binary variable) and the row label 'Competitive pressure' in Tables 3-4
levels.rationale: Text-table conflict; the dummy cut point is not stated.

levels.description: Dummy = 1 if V328 >= 3 (moderate or a great deal).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Alternative dichotomization
levels.rationale: Not described.

axes.decision: Industry fixed effects

levels.description: Two-digit 1972 SIC major-group dummies obtained by mapping V43/INDUSTRY (1980 Census industry codes) through the supplied crosswalk (sic2_from_printed; first listed group when a Census category spans several SIC groups; not-specified categories assigned to the nearest listed group or treated as their own group); one group omitted.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p12 ('33 dummy variables representing two-digit SIC industries'); source description (no SIC variable in the release); census1980_industry_sic1972_README.md
levels.rationale: Reproduces the stated classification; the authors' own mapping is unknown, so the number of groups may differ from the article's count.

levels.description: Dummies for the 1980 Census industry codes themselves (V43), collapsed to the Census sector headings (about 13 groups).
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: Dictionary (INDUSTRY label); crosswalk sector_heading column
levels.rationale: Coarser industry control than the article's two-digit SIC.

levels.description: Use INDUSTRY instead of V43 as the source code.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: Dictionary note: file-creation syntax sets V43 = INDUSTRY
levels.rationale: Identical values by construction.

axes.decision: Covariance estimator

levels.description: Conventional OLS standard errors.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p15 footnote a ('standard errors in parentheses'); no robust or clustered method mentioned anywhere
levels.rationale: Default for the method and period.

levels.description: Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: White (1980) type corrections; standard methodological alternative
levels.rationale: Coefficients identical; SEs and stars would not match the printed ones by construction.

levels.description: Standard errors clustered on distinct establishment (for duplicate records) when A01 = L0.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: NOS duplicate-employer documentation
levels.rationale: Addresses dependence created by copied records; not described.

axes.decision: Sampling weights

levels.description: Unweighted OLS.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p5-6 describe the size-proportional design but no weighting is mentioned in Methods or Results
levels.rationale: Silence plus 'multiple regression' implies unweighted.

levels.description: WLS with WEIGHT (inverse of establishment size) to represent establishments rather than employees.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: nos1991_source_description.md (weights undo probability-proportional-to-size selection)
levels.rationale: Changes the estimand to the establishment population; not what the article reports.

axes.decision: Interaction-term construction

levels.description: Raw products of the two indices.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p11 (Venkatraman 1989 moderated/interactive relationship); no centering mentioned
levels.rationale: Default; main-effect coefficients in the interaction models are conditional on zero of the partner variable.

levels.description: Products of mean-centered indices.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Aiken & West (1991)-style practice
levels.rationale: Interaction coefficient and its test identical to L0; main-effect coefficients and constant differ, so main-effect targets in Models 4, 5, 9, 10 would not match.

axes.decision: Vertical hierarchy: logarithm base and top code

levels.description: Natural log of V261; code 96 ('100 or more') treated as 100.
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p10 Table 1 footnote c ('Value is a logarithm'); D1 p11 uses 'natural logarithm' for employment; dictionary Q.69 code 96
levels.rationale: Consistent with the article's other log usage; the top code rule is inferred.

levels.description: Base-10 log of V261.
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Footnote c does not state the base
levels.rationale: Changes the coefficient scale by a constant factor; significance identical.

levels.description: Code 96 treated as missing.
levels.label: equivalent
levels.source: Dictionary (96 not declared missing)
levels.rationale: Affects at most a handful of extreme cases.

axes.decision: Outcome scoring

levels.description: Mean of reversed items (1-4 scale).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p7 (items 'ranging from 1 worse to 4 much better'); Table 1 range 1-4; Table 2 means on that scale
levels.rationale: Printed descriptives are on the item scale.

levels.description: Sum of reversed items.
levels.label: non_equivalent
levels.source: Common alternative scoring
levels.rationale: Coefficients scaled by the item count; not comparable to printed values.

axes.decision: Treatment of V41 = 4 ('neither' product nor service) for the product/service dummies

levels.description: Treat 'neither' as missing (drop).
levels.label: origin
levels.source: D1 p12 (omitted category defined as 'both products and services' only)
levels.rationale: Keeps the omitted category as described.

levels.description: Code 'neither' with both dummies zero (merged into the omitted category).
levels.label: uncertain
levels.source: Default dummy construction
levels.rationale: Not described; affects few cases.

compatibility_notes: Models 2 and 3 (and 7 and 8) differ only by swapping internal labor market for vertical hierarchy; they are distinct reported models, not alternative specifications of one another. The explicit control list (nonprofit where applicable, subsidiary, log employment, log age, percent managers, union pressure, product, service, competition, two-digit SIC dummies) is fixed within the equivalent set; no level above adds or removes a control. A02 L1 changes the Table 4 population and should be run, if at all, as a separate branch. A03 L0 must be combined with any A04/A08 choice because the index missing rule determines the common sample. A13 L1 and A16 L1 are text-vs-table conflicts: implementers should run the table-consistent level as origin and report the text level as a flagged branch. A18 and A19 alter inference or estimand only and are not part of the equivalent set.
